name: edit_track
description:
Manage tracks. Actions: list | create | update | delete | tighten.

# Effects

Effects attached to tracks (including Linear Mask) are effect items. Add or change them with edit_item using type:"effect" and their effect item ID. edit_track does not update effect propertyOverrides.

# Roles & ducking

Auto-ducking comes from per-track roles — aim for ONE role per track, on the track that actually contains the relevant clips (talking-head speech often lives on the main video track's embedded audio, e.g. V1, not A1; put music below the speech-bearing track). "anchor" = voice/speech track whose item ranges trigger ducking; "follower" = BGM/music track automatically lowered where its items overlap anchor items; "role":null turns ducking off. For speech clarity, use roles instead of item-level music gain changes. Leave "audioRouting.duckDepthDb" unset so the tool derives depth from timeline loudness; pass it only when the user explicitly wants the music louder/softer under speech, and duckDepthDb:null to clear a manual value.

- list: return the current track order with stable ids and aliases. Read-only; prefer this when you need to discover the latest aliases before another edit.
- create: create one or more tracks. JSON: {"trackType":"video"} or {"trackType":"video","count":4} (order defaults after existing tracks, which is visually on top for video). Pass "order":N as a zero-based list position; for video tracks, lower order / V1 is behind, higher order / larger V alias renders on top. Audio is inverted: A1 (lowest order) is the top lane, and higher order sits below. The result includes stable track ids; use those ids for follow-up item/caption edits because aliases like V1/V2 can shift when inserting tracks. Optional "role" / "name" / "audioRouting" per # Roles & ducking.
- update: change order, hidden, muted, role, name, or audioRouting. For order, pass a zero-based list position; for video overlays, use the highest-order video track / largest V alias to render above existing video. Role and duckDepthDb semantics per # Roles & ducking; note "role":"follower" reinitializes duck depth unless you pass an explicit duckDepthDb. The result includes the resulting track order with stable ids and aliases.
- delete: remove an empty track only — it is refused while clips, track effect, layouts, zooms, or adjustment clips still live on that track. For several empty tracks, use ONE call via trackIds (never one call per track). All refs are resolved and preflighted against the current state before anything is deleted, so passing V2 and V3 together is safe even though aliases renumber after each removal. A batch must stay on one timeline. The result includes the remaining track order with stable ids and aliases.
- tighten: close gaps between items on the track by snapping each item to the end of the previous one.

action.description: list, create, update, delete, or tighten

json.description: JSON for create/update, e.g. {"trackType":"video"} or {"trackType":"audio","role":"follower"} or {"role":"anchor"} or {"role":null} or {"audioRouting":{"duckDepthDb":null}}

projectId.description: Existing project ID from the editor URL or list_projects. Pass this when continuing work on an existing project and the external MCP session is not already targeted.

trackId.description: Track alias (V1, A1) or ID (for update/delete/tighten)

trackIds.description: delete: several track aliases/ids removed in one call. Use this instead of repeated single deletes.
